[2026-11-13] c:6860305827 comment by javierpmateos:
Tested f19656b

Built with `-DABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME`. `mempool_truc.py` passes, including the new `test_truc_reorg_no_sibling_eviction` test.

I ran 1,200 iterations with my two-node randomized reorg test (4 seeds, 3 configurations). This covered BIP68, double-spends, TRUC, coinbase spends, reorgs up to 20 blocks, and the invalid-block case where cleanup runs at a lower intermediate tip. About 10k transactions were in the disconnected blocks. Neither `Assume()` failed.

I also checked that the checks actually fire. Making the mempool size check fail caused an abort right away. Removing `TX_MISSING_INPUTS` or `TX_PREMATURE_SPEND` from the allowed rejection cases also caused aborts (the latter with the coinbase variants). Reverted everything after each check.

I didn't run or review the fuzzing changes, and haven't covered all the rejection cases yet (cluster limits, non-standard, witness).

Scripts: https://gist.github.com/javierpmateos/358865d350735dd76bcf821b1fe1cac4 (`mempool_reorg_twonode_random.py`)
</new_statements>
